compatibility.title: Which Volkswagen Models Use the CUNA?
compatibility.intro: The CUNA engine code was specifically developed for high-performance, premium diesel applications within the Volkswagen Group. Its 184hp output made it the definitive choice for "GTI-equivalent" diesel models, primarily the Volkswagen Golf GTD and the Audi A3 2.0 TDI, during the Mk7 / 8V generation cycle.

costGuide.title: Volkswagen CUNA Engine Replacement Cost (UK)
costGuide.labourLine: Fitting a CUNA typically takes 8-11 hours at £65/hr (independent specialist rate) - confirm exact labour when comparing quotes.
paragraphs: The CUNA’s 184hp output means it is frequently subjected to harder, performance-oriented driving, making turbocharger health and DPF condition the primary drivers of replacement cost. A unit with a documented history of regular AdBlue system maintenance and recent DPF regeneration cycles will command the higher end of the reconditioned price spectrum. For a complete breakdown of how condition affects pricing, see our full reconditioned engine cost guide.

failures.title: Volkswagen CUNA Engine Problems - What Actually Fails

items.title: AdBlue System & NOx Sensor Failures - 2013-2020
items.whatHappens: The EA288 architecture’s emissions control system is prone to NOx sensor faults and AdBlue heater element failures. This triggers dashboard warnings, forces the vehicle into limp mode, and can eventually prevent the engine from restarting once the ignition is cycled.
items.repairVsReplace: Isolated sensor or heater failures are often resolved with component replacement and software updates (£400-£1,500). However, if the AdBlue fault is accompanied by severe DPF blockage, the cumulative repair cost often makes a full CUNA engine replacement the more economical long-term solution.

items.title: DPF Clogging (Urban Use) - 2013-2020
items.whatHappens: Frequent short journeys prevent the diesel particulate filter from reaching the high temperatures required for active regeneration. This leads to ash buildup, restricted exhaust flow, elevated exhaust gas temperatures, and eventual secondary strain on the turbocharger and EGR cooler.
items.repairVsReplace: Professional off-car DPF cleaning can resolve early-stage blockages. However, severe clogging combined with EGR cooler leaks or turbo degradation typically necessitates a reconditioned replacement to restore reliable performance.

failures.goodYearsLine: The EA288 family, including the CUNA, is generally considered significantly more robust and reliable than the preceding EA189 generation, with far fewer timing chain stretch and injector failure issues reported in post-2013 units .

variants.title: How to Confirm You Have the CUNA
variants.intro: The CUNA engine code is stamped on a machined pad on the engine block, typically located near the oil filter housing or on the upper timing belt cover. It is also clearly listed on your vehicle’s V5C registration document under "Engine Number" and can be definitively verified via a VIN decode.

relatives.description: - The early common-rail EA189 unit it replaced lacked complex AdBlue systems but suffered from higher rates of injector coking and DPF blockage.
- The EA288 Ultra successor focused on maximum efficiency and lower emissions, sharing the same fundamental block architecture but with different turbo and calibration mapping.
- If your vehicle is a standard 150hp model rather than the 184hp GTD variant, consult the CRLB page, as the turbocharger, ECU mapping, and exhaust plumbing are not direct swaps.

buyingGuide.title: Buying a Replacement CUNA - What to Choose

options.label: Used
options.body: A used CUNA is only advisable if it comes with a comprehensive, stamped service history proving regular DPF regenerations and AdBlue system maintenance. Given its 184hp performance tuning, previous owners may have driven the vehicle hard, making a low-mileage used unit with documented care the only safe used purchase. Compare used CUNA engines

options.label: Reconditioned
options.body: This is the highly recommended route for the CUNA. A proper reconditioning process will proactively replace the AdBlue dosing unit, NOx sensors, and DPF, while also upgrading the oil pump and timing components to prevent common EA288 wear patterns, delivering near-new reliability. Compare reconditioned CUNA engines

options.label: Rebuilt
options.body: A full rebuild is justified if the CUNA has suffered catastrophic turbo failure that sent debris into the cylinders, or if the vehicle is a high-value Golf GTD or Audi A3 intended for long-term ownership. An upgraded rebuild should include a revised turbocharger and reinforced head gasket. Compare rebuilt CUNA engines

buyingGuide.supplyFitLine: Securing a CUNA through our network guarantees a minimum 12-month warranty, with nationwide delivery and the option for vetted local specialist fitting to ensure the job is done right the first time. Explore supply and fit options
buyingGuide.vehicleValueNote: For typical host vehicles like the Volkswagen Golf Mk7 GTD or Audi A3 8V, current UK market values range from £5,000 to £16,000. items.question: How much does a Volkswagen CUNA engine replacement cost?
items.answer: A reconditioned Volkswagen CUNA engine costs between £2,800 and £4,500 for supply-only, or £3,320 to £5,215 fully fitted by an independent specialist . This pricing reflects the high-performance nature of the 184hp tune. Supply-only options allow for independent specialist fitting to manage overall labour costs. Get CUNA engine replacement quotes

items.question: What is the most common Volkswagen CUNA engine failure?
items.answer: The most documented failure pattern involves the AdBlue system and NOx sensor faults, frequently accompanied by DPF clogging in urban driving conditions. These emissions components are under higher stress in the 184hp GTD variant due to performance-oriented driving cycles. Compare rebuilt CUNA prices with emissions systems addressed

items.question: Which car models use the Volkswagen CUNA engine?
items.answer: The CUNA engine code is fitted exclusively to high-performance diesel variants, primarily the Volkswagen Golf Mk7 GTD and the Audi A3 8V 2.0 TDI (184hp) manufactured between 2013 and 2020. It was not used in standard trim levels. Check your exact CUNA fitment by registration

items.question: Should I buy a used or reconditioned CUNA engine?
items.answer: A reconditioned CUNA is highly recommended over a used unit. Given the known risks of AdBlue degradation and DPF saturation in performance-driven hosts, a professionally reconditioned unit ensures these critical emissions components are renewed or tested, preventing immediate repeat failures. items.answer: You can confirm the CUNA engine code by checking the vehicle’s V5C registration document under "Engine Number" or by locating the stamped code on the engine block near the oil filter housing. Do not rely solely on the vehicle badge, as trim levels can be misleading. Enter your reg to confirm your CUNA fitment
